main_issue: Whether D's medical alert bracelet must come off under the new no-visible-jewellery rule, or can stay on (covered) for tomorrow's shift

A-B.evidence: B raised the question (T2) without taking a side; at T14-15 A asks if all are clear and B says 'Yeah, clear', accepting the covered-bracelet solution.

A-C.evidence: A insisted it must come off (T3, T6) while C objected (T5, T7); A then accepted covering it (T9) and C said 'I'm clear' (T17).

A-D.evidence: A said the bracelet must come off (T3); D proposed covering it (T8); A agreed 'If we can't see it, that's fine' (T9); D accepted (T10, T13).

B-C.evidence: B raised the bracelet question (T2) and C defended the bracelet (T5, T7); both later said they were clear (T15, T17) with the covered solution. They did not address each other directly.

B-D.evidence: B asked about D's bracelet (T2) without taking a side; at T15 B says 'clear' after D's covering plan was accepted. They did not speak to each other.

C-D.evidence: C argued the bracelet is medical, not jewellery (T5, T7), supporting D's need to wear it; D's covering plan (T8) was accepted and C said clear (T17).
